subject: spider
readings: Head end at +x: the cephalothorax (bearing all 8 leg attachments and the mouth/eyes) sits at the +x end of the mesh; the abdomen trails at -x. XY panel is the profile (side view, shows the classic tarantula leg-arch), ZY panel is the front view (legs symmetric left/right), XZ panel is the top view (shows leg splay and fore-aft attachment order).

XY panel: cephalothorax center ≈ (19,9); abdomen center ≈ (9,11); abdomen rear tip ≈ (3,13). Abdomen extends ~16 units behind the cephalothorax and droops slightly (screen dy ~+2 downward → frame dy small negative).

XY panel: ground line (bottom of all feet) ≈ y=15.5; cephalothorax dorsal surface ≈ y=7, so legs rise ~8 units above their hip before descending ~8-9 units back to the ground, matching the visible elbow-bend silhouette.
XY panel front leg (pair1): hip ≈ (21,8), elbow/knee ≈ (24,5) [screen y decreases → frame dy positive, leg rises], foot ≈ (22,15) [screen y increases a lot → frame dy strongly negative].

XZ panel (top view): cephalothorax spans x≈14-24, z center ≈12; legs splay outward to z≈2 and z≈22 at their widest (pair 1/2), while the hindmost pair (4) reaches back to x≈2, crossing behind the abdomen, confirming hind legs are the longest and most posterior.
ZY panel (front view): body center z≈11-12; legs symmetric about this center, tips reaching z≈0 and z≈24; all feet converge to ground y≈15-16, consistent with the XY ground reading.
Four hip positions read along the cephalothorax long axis in XZ/XY panels: leg1≈x22 (front), leg2≈x19.5, leg3≈x17, leg4≈x14.5 (rear, nearest abdomen junction).
notes: Subject is a spider: cephalothorax (prosoma) and abdomen (opisthosoma) are fused-body trunk nodes, not leaves, per the carapace rule. Pedipalps are present but small/leg-like and per the 'four leg pairs, never five' rule are not given a leaf. All 8 legs (4 pairs, L/R) are each split into 3 inferred segments (coxa->hip, femur->knee, tibia+tarsus->foot) to capture the clear elbow-arch silhouette visible in the XY profile; this segmentation is an anatomical inference, not a directly measured joint. Leg lengths were kept nearly equal per pair per the proportion-not-pose rule, with the hindmost pair (4) given slightly greater length since the XZ top view shows it reaching furthest posteriorly/laterally past the abdomen, a proportional (not merely postural) difference typical of tarantulas. All descending segments (elbow->foot) were given negative dy to match the ground being a larger screen-y value than the body/hip, per the required sign flip. Left/right assigned as +z/-z arbitrarily but consistently; front-to-back leg order taken from hip x-positions read off the XZ/XY panels.
